thread:
maria: Heads up — I'm seeing a cluster-wide uptick in Xid errors in eu-west1 starting ~07:10 UTC, but card temps look stable. No sustained thermal trend. Suspect network/PCIe link resets or firmware hiccups. Can we add netlink and PCIe link flap signals to the gpu-health Grafana panels and adjust the healthscore to surface non-thermal failures? Also proposing a small runbook addendum: probe NIC interrupts + dmesg for link_reset before draining.
aj: Noted. Can you drop the exact Prometheus queries you used so we can start correlating with pod eviction logs?
maria: Sure — rough queries I ran:

```promql
sum by(card_id) (increase(nvml_xid_errors_total[1h]))
sum by(card_id) (increase(node_network_receive_drop_total[1h]))
sum by(card_id) (increase(node_pcie_link_flap_total[1h]))

# correlate with evictions
sum by(card_id) (increase(kube_pod_evictions_total{reason="GPU_PRESSURE"}[1h]))
```

We should surface these side-by-side per-card and add a label_join to map card_id -> rack so ops can prioritize.
kevin: If link flaps are the culprit, we should avoid over-weighting thermal signals for those cards. Maybe add a `failure_mode` tag in the healthscore pipeline (thermal | link | firmware | other) so downstream runbooks can pick appropriate remediation.
nisha: Sampling note: to keep log retention/cost manageable, only capture full dmesg/kernel logs for cards that exceed >5 Xid events in 30m. For 1-4 Xids we can keep condensed counts and a short trace. +1 on adding the network panels.
ops-bot: Deployment: Draft grafana patch created for dashboard `gpu-health` — panels: Xid per-card, net drops, pcie_link_flaps, evictions. Link: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd1234/gpu-health (draft)
aj: Quick question on SLOs — are we proposing a change to customer-facing SLOs or internal reliability weighting? We need to avoid surprise changes.
maria: This is internal infra weighting only — not customer-facing. Proposal: shift 10% of the internal healthscore weight from thermal to link/firmware buckets for the next 2-week evaluation window so detection/triage surfaces different root causes. I'll open PRs for the scoring change + runbook addendum. ETA EOD for PR; will ping for review.
ryan: If we enable automatic drains based on this new mode, add a short cooldown (e.g., 10m) and a backoff so we don't thrash cards that are recovering. Also consider a temporary quota-based bypass for critical reserved pools.
maria: Good call. I'll include cooldown/backoff params in the runbook and dashboard (a small panel showing recent drains + cooldown state). Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
